subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron `agentTurn` runs get a first-class hard tool policy, and if so should it be a new `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` surface or inheritance from `tools.subagents.tools`?
rationale: This is a public config and security-boundary decision with compatibility impact across cron delivery, per-job allowlists, inherited creator caps, and CLI backends, so automation should not choose the permanent policy shape.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence, docs, schema metadata, and tests for announce/webhook/none delivery plus CLI and embedded runtime behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron sessions explicitly inherit `tools.subagents.tools` if maintainers want one delegated-execution policy instead of another top-level config surface.

options.title: Keep per-job policy only
options.body: Leave global cron policy out of core and rely on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards, accepting that operators cannot set a central cron denylist.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence, docs, schema metadata, and tests for announce/webhook/none delivery plus CLI and embedded runtime behavior.
